record.paper_title: Open Problems in Geometry and Topology
record.context_brief: Moore conjecture on p-torsion in homotopy groups
record.original_question: Let X be a simply connected finite CW complex. Suppose the rational homotopy groups are finite-dimensional in the sense that dim(π_*(X) ⊗ Q) is finite. For each prime p, does there exist an integer k such that multiplication by p^k annihilates the p-torsion in π_*(X)?

evidence.quote: The following is a question asked by John Moore about homotopy groups: Suppose that X is a simply connected, finite complex. If dim(π*(X) ⊗ Q) is finite, is there, for each prime p, and integer k for which p^k annihilates the p-torsion in π*(X)?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $X$ be a simply connected finite CW complex, and assume that the total rational homotopy of $X$ is finite-dimensional, i.e.
$$\dim_{\mathbb{Q}}\bigl(\pi_*(X)\otimes \mathbb{Q}\bigr) < \infty.$$
(Equivalently, $X$ is rationally elliptic.) For a prime $p$, the $p$-torsion subgroup of $\pi_*(X)$ is the set of elements of $p$-power order in the graded abelian group $\pi_*(X)=\bigoplus_{n\ge 2}\pi_n(X)$.

Question: For every prime $p$, does there exist a positive integer $k=k(X,p)$ such that multiplication by $p^k$ annihilates the entire $p$-torsion subgroup of $\pi_*(X)$?
artifact.status_search_result: Moore's conjecture on homotopy exponents remains open in general. Recent work (e.g., on polyhedral products, Poincaré duality complexes, connected sums, and 2-cones) has established the conjecture in particular families of spaces or at all but finitely many primes, but no general proof exists.

status_evidence.title: Local hyperbolicity, inert maps and applications in Moore's conjecture
status_evidence.snippet: Intensive progress on Moore's conjecture has been made for Poincaré duality complexes and generalized moment-angle complexes...
status_evidence.claim: Moore's conjecture is the subject of ongoing partial progress, indicating it is not settled in general.

status_evidence.title: Moore's conjecture for connected sums
status_evidence.snippet: Moore's Conjecture states that a finite simply connected CW complex has a homotopy exponent at p if and only if it has totally finite rational homotopy.
status_evidence.claim: The conjecture is verified only in special cases such as connected sums, supporting that the general statement is still open.

status_evidence.title: Moore's conjecture for polyhedral products
status_evidence.snippet: An elliptic space has a finite exponent at all but finitely many primes; a 2-cone satisfies Moore's conjecture at all but finitely many primes.
status_evidence.claim: Only partial results are known for elliptic spaces in general.
